papers.title: First report of human infection caused by swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v virus in mainland China: a confirmed case identified through influenza-like illness surveillance, Kunming (Yunnan), 2025
papers.abstract: Objective This case report details the epidemiological characteristics of the first human case of swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v infection identified in mainland China, to formulate guidelines for the prevention and control of human swine-origin influenza A (H1N2) virus infections. Methods Clinical and epidemiological data of the case were collected through field epidemiological investigation combined with laboratory testing. Specimens were collected from the patient, close contacts, animals subjects (including one deceased pig), and environmental matrices and analyzed to trace the potential infection source and characterize the clinical and epidemiological features. Results This study describes a sporadic, isolated case of human infection with swine influenza A(H1N2)v in mainland China, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission. Prior to symptom onset, the patient inhabited a high-risk mixed residential setting with frequent close exposure to domestic livestock and poultry. Specially, his townhouse stood adjacent to his great-uncle’s residence, where swine were raised; the great-uncle also documented the mortality of one pig. But had no contact with human confirmed cases presenting similar clinical manifestations. Testing of the collected specimens confirmed influenza N2 subtype positivity in lung tissue specimens obtained from the deceased pigs, whereas all remaining animal and environmental specimens yielded negative test results. The patient was eventually discharged after clinical recovery. A total of 30 close contacts completed self-health monitoring and throat swab screening. No influenza-like illness developed among these individuals throughout the monitoring period, and all throat swab specimens yielded negative test results. No secondary cases were detected during medical monitoring, and targeted environmental disinfection was implemented accordingly. Conclusion The likely source of infection for the reported case was identified as deceased pigs harboring N2-subtype influenza A virus. Therefore, enhanced surveillance of novel influenza subtypes such as A(H1N2)v and improved swine influenza vaccination are crucial for the targeted prevention and control of human infections by these emerging viruses.

papers.source_body_en: Objective This case report details the epidemiological characteristics of the first human case of swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v infection identified in mainland China, to formulate guidelines for the prevention and control of human swine-origin influenza A (H1N2) virus infections. Methods Clinical and epidemiological data of the case were collected through field epidemiological investigation combined with laboratory testing. Specimens were collected from the patient, close contacts, animals subjects (including one deceased pig), and environmental matrices and analyzed to trace the potential infection source and characterize the clinical and epidemiological features. Results This study describes a sporadic, isolated case of human infection with swine influenza A(H1N2)v in mainland China, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission. Prior to symptom onset, the patient inhabited a high-risk mixed residential setting with frequent close exposure to domestic livestock and poultry. Specially, his townhouse stood adjacent to his great-uncle’s residence, where swine were raised; the great-uncle also documented the mortality of one pig. But had no contact with human confirmed cases presenting similar clinical manifestations. Testing of the collected specimens confirmed influenza N2 subtype positivity in lung tissue specimens obtained from the deceased pigs, whereas all remaining animal and environmental specimens yielded negative test results. The patient was eventually discharged after clinical recovery. A total of 30 close contacts completed self-health monitoring and throat swab screening. No influenza-like illness developed among these individuals throughout the monitoring period, and all throat swab specimens yielded negative test results. No secondary cases were detected during medical monitoring, and targeted environmental disinfection was implemented accordingly. Conclusion The likely source of infection for the reported case was identified as deceased pigs harboring N2-subtype influenza A virus. Therefore, enhanced surveillance of novel influenza subtypes such as A(H1N2)v and improved swine influenza vaccination are crucial for the targeted prevention and control of human infections by these emerging viruses.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 详细介绍中国大陆首例人源甲型H1N2流感病毒感染病例的流行病学特征,为制定人源性甲型H1N2流感病毒感染防控指南提供依据。方法通过现场流行病学调查结合实验室检测,收集该病例的临床和流行病学资料。从患者、密切接触者、动物受试者(包括一头死猪)和环境基质中收集样本并进行分析,以追踪潜在的感染源并描述临床和流行病学特征。结果本研究描述了中国大陆发生的一例散发性、孤立的人感染甲型H1N2猪流感病例,没有人传人传播的证据。症状出现前,患者居住在高风险混合住宅环境中,经常近距离接触家畜和家禽。特别是,他的联排别墅毗邻他叔公的住所,那里养猪;叔公还记录了一只猪的死亡率。但没有接触过出现类似临床表现的人类确诊病例。对收集的样本进行检测证实,从死猪身上获得的肺组织样本中呈流感 N2 亚型阳性,而所有剩余的动物和环境样本的检测结果均为阴性。患者最终在临床康复后出院。共有30名密切接触者完成自我健康监测和咽拭子筛查。在整个监测期间,这些人没有出现流感样疾病,所有咽拭子样本检测结果均为阴性。医学监测未发现继发病例,并相应实施了有针对性的环境消毒。结论 初步判断该病例的可能传染源为携带N2亚型甲型流感病毒的死猪。因此,A(H1N2)v等新型流感亚型的增强型监测和改良型猪流感疫苗接种对于有针对性地预防和控制这些新兴病毒引起的人类感染至关重要。

papers.title: SNHG15 Positively Regulates Influenza Virus Infection Through Its Association With miR-153 and RABL2A.
papers.abstract: Influenza viruses cause seasonal epidemics, and current vaccines do not fully protect against them. This study focuses on long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are RNA molecules that do not code for proteins but play crucial roles in various biological processes. We identified 17 lncRNAs altered by the influenza virus. Among these, SNHG15 was found to enhance influenza virus infection. Knockdown of SNHG15 using CRISPR interference and RNA interference reduced influenza virus infection, while overexpression of SNHG15 increased virus replication. We found that miR-153-3p, a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for SNHG15, acts as an anti-influenza microRNA, and its overexpression negated SNHG15's proviral activity. RNA pull-down and mass spectrometry identified Rab-like protein 2A (RABL2A) as an interacting partner of SNHG15. Both SNHG15 and RABL2A facilitated influenza virus internalization. Additionally, siRNA-mediated knockdown of RABL2A reduced SNHG15-mediated virus internalization. In conclusion, SNHG15 enhances influenza A virus infection through its interactions with miR-153 and RABL2A.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感病毒引起季节性流行,目前的 疫苗 并不能完全预防流感病毒。这项研究重点关注长链非编码 RNA (lncRNA),它们是不编码蛋白质但在各种生物过程中发挥关键作用的 RNA 分子。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究鉴定了 17 个被流感病毒改变的 lncRNA,重点关注 SNHG15 在增强流感病毒感染方面的作用。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 CRISPR 干扰和 RNA 干扰敲低 SNHG15 可减少流感病毒感染,而 SNHG15 过度表达可增加病毒复制。RNA Pull-down 和质谱鉴定出 Rab 样蛋白 2A (RABL2A) 是 SNHG15 的相互作用伙伴。
elements_zh.main_results: 在改变的lncRNA中,SNHG15被发现可以增强流感病毒感染。SNHG15 的敲低减少了流感病毒的感染,而过度表达则增加了病毒的复制。SNHG15 和 RABL2A 均促进流感病毒内化。

papers.source_body_en: Influenza viruses cause seasonal epidemics, and current vaccines do not fully protect against them. This study focuses on long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are RNA molecules that do not code for proteins but play crucial roles in various biological processes. We identified 17 lncRNAs altered by the influenza virus. Among these, SNHG15 was found to enhance influenza virus infection. Knockdown of SNHG15 using CRISPR interference and RNA interference reduced influenza virus infection, while overexpression of SNHG15 increased virus replication. We found that miR-153-3p, a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for SNHG15, acts as an anti-influenza microRNA, and its overexpression negated SNHG15's proviral activity. RNA pull-down and mass spectrometry identified Rab-like protein 2A (RABL2A) as an interacting partner of SNHG15. Both SNHG15 and RABL2A facilitated influenza virus internalization. Additionally, siRNA-mediated knockdown of RABL2A reduced SNHG15-mediated virus internalization. In conclusion, SNHG15 enhances influenza A virus infection through its interactions with miR-153 and RABL2A.

papers.title: Vaccine Literacy, Knowledge, and Acceptance Among University Students in the West Bank, Palestine: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study of Health and Non-Health Students
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Vaccine hesitancy remains a significant public health challenge globally, and vaccine literacy is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of vaccine acceptance. Data on vaccine literacy and acceptance among university students in Palestine are scarce, and no study has directly compared these outcomes across health and non-health disciplines in this setting. This study aimed to assess vaccine literacy, knowledge, and acceptance among Palestinian university students and identify associated factors with vaccine acceptance. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted at multiple universities across the West Bank, Palestine, during the 2025–2026 academic year. A total of 633 university students completed a structured, self-administered questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. The instrument comprised four sections assessing sociodemographic characteristics, vaccination history and information sources, vaccine knowledge (10 binary items), and vaccine literacy and acceptance using validated five-point Likert scales. Non-parametric group comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test and Chi-square test. Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression were used to identify predictors of vaccine acceptance. Results The median age of participants was 19 years (IQR: 18–21), and 72.4% were female. Median scores were moderate across all domains: vaccine knowledge 5.0/10 (IQR: 3.0–6.0), vaccine literacy 3.50/5 (IQR: 3.0–3.88), and vaccine acceptance 3.11/5 (IQR: 2.78–3.56). While 67.8% of students reported receiving recommended vaccines in the past five years, seasonal influenza vaccination was critically low at 9.5%. Health-related students scored significantly higher than non-health students in knowledge, literacy, acceptance, vaccine uptake, and trust in official sources (all p ≤ 0.010). analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted at multiple universities across the West Bank, Palestine, during the 2025–2026 academic year, involving 633 university students who completed a structured, self-administered questionnaire distributed via Google Forms.
analysis.methods: Non-parametric group comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test and Chi-square test, while Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression were used to identify predictors of vaccine acceptance.
analysis.main_results: The median age of participants was 19 years (IQR: 18–21), and 72.4% were female; median scores were moderate across all domains: vaccine knowledge 5.0/10 (IQR: 3.0–6.0), vaccine literacy 3.50/5 (IQR: 3.0–3.88), and vaccine acceptance 3.11/5 (IQR: 2.78–3.56); while 67.8% of students reported receiving recommended vaccines in the past five years, seasonal influenza vaccination was critically low at 9.5%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Health-related students scored significantly higher than non-health students in knowledge, literacy, acceptance, vaccine uptake, and trust in official sources (all p ≤ 0.010), and female students demonstrated higher knowledge (p = 0.021) and literacy scores (p < 0.05).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccine literacy and acceptance among university students in Palestine, particularly for seasonal influenza vaccination, which remains critically low.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce recall bias; however, the large sample size and validated instruments provide moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025-2026 学年,巴勒斯坦西岸多所大学进行了一项横断面研究,涉及 633 名大学生,他们完成了通过 Google Forms 分发的结构化、自填式调查问卷。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Mann–Whitney U 检验和卡方检验进行非参数组比较,同时使用 Spearman 相关性和多变量线性回归来确定 疫苗 接受度的预测因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 参与者的中位年龄为 19 岁(IQR:18-21),其中 72.4% 为女性;所有领域的中位数得分均中等:疫苗 知识 5.0/10(IQR:3.0–6.0)、疫苗 读写能力 3.50/5(IQR:3.0–3.88)和 疫苗 接受度 3.11/5(IQR:2.78–3.56);虽然 67.8% 的学生表示在过去五年中收到了推荐的 疫苗,但 季节性流感 疫苗接种 的比例极低,仅为 9.5%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 健康相关学生在知识、读写能力、接受度、疫苗 吸收和对官方来源的信任方面的得分显着高于非健康学生(p ≤ 0.010),并且女学生表现出更高的知识(p = 0.021)和读写能力得分(p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要采取有针对性的干预措施来提高巴勒斯坦大学生的 疫苗 识字率和接受度,特别是 季节性流感 疫苗接种,其水平仍然极低。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计的限制,无法建立因果关系,并且依赖自我报告的数据,可能会引入回忆偏差;然而,大样本量和经过验证的仪器提供了中等的证据强度。

papers.title: Social influence versus fear in COVID-19 vaccine acceptance: insights for health marketing communication
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how fear (of COVID-19 and of COVID-19 vaccine side effects) and social influence jointly and individually affect the intention to receive the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine. This study aims to fill a gap in health and pharmaceutical marketing research by clarifying the relative importance of emotional versus social drivers of vaccine acceptance. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 600 adults residing in Spain was conducted using quota sampling for age and gender (gender quotas were partially unmet). Respondents evaluated fear of COVID-19, fear of vaccine side effects, social influence and intention to vaccinate using established scales. Consistent partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to assess measurement validity and to compare three models: a joint model including all predictors, a fear-only model and a social-influence-only model. Findings Fear of COVID-19 has a positive effect on vaccination intention, while fear of vaccine side effects has a negative effect. Social influence shows a strong positive effect and is the most influential predictor across all models. When considered jointly, social influence substantially reduces the explanatory power of fear, indicating that trusted individuals and institutions shape vaccination decisions more decisively than emotional responses. Research limitations/implications Results are limited to Spain and to the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine during a specific time period. Replication in other countries, vaccine types and socio-economic contexts is recommended. Nevertheless, the findings may be particularly relevant for contexts similar to that generated by the COVID-19 pandemic, in which both the disease and the potential effects of the vaccine were largely unknown, resulting in levels of uncertainty substantially higher than those associated with well-established diseases and vaccines, such as seasonal influenza. Practical implications Health communication and pharmaceutical marketing strategies should prioritize credible institutional messaging and trusted influencers rather than fear-based appeals. Addressing misinformation and strengthening institutional trust are essential. Originality/value This study offers an original analytical focus by providing the first comparative analysis of joint versus individual effects of fear and social influence on COVID-19 vaccination intention, offering new insights for health marketing strategy design.
papers.journal: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本文研究了恐惧(对 COVID-19 和 COVID-19 疫苗 副作用)和社会影响如何共同和单独影响接受牛津-阿斯利康 疫苗 的意图,旨在通过澄清 疫苗 接受的情感与社会驱动因素的相对重要性,填补健康和药品营销研究的空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用年龄和性别配额抽样对居住在西班牙的 600 名成年人进行了定量调查(性别配额部分未得到满足)。
elements_zh.methods: 受访者使用既定量表评估了对 COVID-19 的恐惧、对 疫苗 副作用的恐惧、社会影响和接种疫苗的意愿,并使用一致的偏最小二乘结构方程模型来评估测量有效性并比较三个模型:包括所有预测因素的联合模型、仅恐惧模型和仅社会影响模型。
elements_zh.main_results: 对 COVID-19 的恐惧对 疫苗接种 意图有积极影响,而对 疫苗 副作用的恐惧则有负面影响。社会影响力显示出强烈的积极影响,并且是所有模型中最具影响力的预测因子。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 综合考虑时,社会影响力大大降低了恐惧的解释力,这表明受信任的个人和机构比情绪反应更能决定性地制定 疫苗接种 决策。这项研究通过首次比较分析恐惧的联合效应与个体效应以及社会对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 意图的影响,提供了一个原创的分析重点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 健康传播和药品营销策略应优先考虑可信的机构信息和值得信赖的影响者,而不是基于恐惧的诉求。解决错误信息和加强机构信任至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 结果仅限于特定时间段内的西班牙和牛津-阿斯利康 疫苗。建议在其他国家、疫苗 类型和社会经济环境中进行复制。

papers.title: FluEvoFormer: A Structure-Guided Generative Foundation Model for Prospective Influenza Antigenic Evolution and Vaccine Strain Selection
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccine strain selection remains challenging because circulating viruses may drift after vaccine recommendations are made. This study presents FluEvoFormer, a structure-guided generative foundation model for prospective influenza antigenic evolution forecasting and vaccine strain ranking. The framework jointly encodes hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences and incorporates residue-contact graphs. Separate prediction heads estimate future viral dominance and the vaccine–virus antigenic match. Controlled future-like variant stress testing, uncertainty adjustments, and clade balancing are then used to rank vaccine candidates. A rolling retrospective evaluation was performed for target seasons involving the influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and influenza A(H3N2) virus. The evaluation used cutoff-restricted sequence records, hemagglutination inhibition data, vaccine-composition records, protein-structure resources, and vaccine-effectiveness indicators. The historical training corpus for the influenza A(H1N1) virus also contained pre-2009 seasonal records. FluEvoFormer achieved the lowest held-out antigenicity prediction error, with mean absolute error (MAE) values of 0.389 for the combined historical influenza A(H1N1) virus corpus and 0.456 for the influenza A(H3N2) virus corpus. It also improved the future dominance prediction, with Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence values of 0.255 and 0.289, respectively. The model selected candidates with higher empirical normalized coverage scores in seven out of 10 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus seasons and nine out of 10 influenza A(H3N2) virus seasons. The predicted coverage score showed a strong positive correlation with external vaccine-effectiveness estimates. These findings support FluEvoFormer as a computational decision-support framework for prioritizing influenza vaccine candidates before downstream laboratory and public health evaluations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性流感 疫苗 菌株选择仍然具有挑战性,因为在提出 疫苗 建议后,循环病毒可能会发生漂移。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究提出了 FluEvoFormer,这是一种结构引导的生成基础模型,用于前瞻性流感抗原 进化 预测和 疫苗 菌株排名。对涉及流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒和流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒的目标季节进行了滚动回顾性评估。
elements_zh.methods: 该框架联合编码血凝素和神经氨酸酶序列并合并残基接触图。单独的预测头估计未来的病毒优势和 疫苗 病毒抗原匹配。然后使用受控的类似未来的变体压力测试、不确定性调整和进化枝平衡来对 疫苗 候选者进行排名。
elements_zh.main_results: FluEvoFormer 实现了最低的保留抗原性预测误差,合并历史甲型 H1N1 流感病毒语料库的平均绝对误差 (MAE) 值为 0.389,流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒语料库的平均绝对误差 (MAE) 值为 0.456。它还改进了未来的优势预测,Kullback-Leibler (KL) 散度值分别为 0.255 和 0.289。该模型在 10 个流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒季节中的 7 个和 10 个流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒季节中的 9 个中选择了具有较高经验归一化覆盖分数的候选者。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 预测的覆盖分数与外部 疫苗 有效性估计呈很强的正相关。这些发现支持 FluEvoFormer 作为计算决策支持框架,用于在下游实验室和公共卫生评估之前优先考虑流感 疫苗 候选者。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: FluEvoFormer 提供了一种计算工具,通过预测抗原 进化 和对候选菌株进行排名来改进流感 疫苗 菌株的选择,从而有可能增强 疫苗 的有效性和公共卫生反应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性评估和历史数据,可能无法完全捕捉未来的病毒 进化 动态。由于仅具有抽象性质并且依赖计算模型而没有现实世界的验证,因此证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: FluEvoFormer:用于前瞻性流感抗原 进化 和 疫苗 菌株选择的结构引导生成基础模型
papers.source_body_en: Seasonal influenza vaccine strain selection remains challenging because circulating viruses may drift after vaccine recommendations are made. This study presents FluEvoFormer, a structure-guided generative foundation model for prospective influenza antigenic evolution forecasting and vaccine strain ranking. The framework jointly encodes hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences and incorporates residue-contact graphs. Separate prediction heads estimate future viral dominance and the vaccine–virus antigenic match. Controlled future-like variant stress testing, uncertainty adjustments, and clade balancing are then used to rank vaccine candidates. A rolling retrospective evaluation was performed for target seasons involving the influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and influenza A(H3N2) virus. The evaluation used cutoff-restricted sequence records, hemagglutination inhibition data, vaccine-composition records, protein-structure resources, and vaccine-effectiveness indicators. The historical training corpus for the influenza A(H1N1) virus also contained pre-2009 seasonal records. FluEvoFormer achieved the lowest held-out antigenicity prediction error, with mean absolute error (MAE) values of 0.389 for the combined historical influenza A(H1N1) virus corpus and 0.456 for the influenza A(H3N2) virus corpus. It also improved the future dominance prediction, with Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence values of 0.255 and 0.289, respectively. The model selected candidates with higher empirical normalized coverage scores in seven out of 10 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus seasons and nine out of 10 influenza A(H3N2) virus seasons. The predicted coverage score showed a strong positive correlation with external vaccine-effectiveness estimates. These findings support FluEvoFormer as a computational decision-support framework for prioritizing influenza vaccine candidates before downstream laboratory and public health evaluations.

papers.title: Multivariate influenza forecasting using time-series foundation models: a comparative study with classical statistical models using 11 years of surveillance data in Hong Kong
papers.abstract: Accurate short-term forecasts of influenza activity are critical for public health preparedness but remain challenging with classical statistical models that depend on long historical data and often fail under data scarcity. Time-series foundation models (TSFMs), pretrained on large heterogeneous datasets, may offer improved accuracy and data efficiency through transferable temporal representations. We analyzed 605 weeks of influenza surveillance data from Hong Kong (2014–2025), including consultation rates, laboratory detections, hospital admissions, severe cases, and school outbreaks. Six TSFMs (Google TimesFM, Amazon Chronos, IBM Granite Tiny Time Mixers [TTM], Timer-XL, Moirai-MoE, and UniTS) were compared with OLS, GLM, SARIMA, and empirical Bayesian models in a rolling-origin design generating one- to four-week forecasts. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using R 2 , RMSE, symmetric MAPE, weighted interval score (WIS) and multivariable residual diagnostics. We further estimated the minimal input window required for R 2 ≥ 0.50 and the maximum credible forecast horizon (R 2 ≥ 0.50 with significant RMSE gain vs. Chronos, TimesFM, and SARIMA achieved the best overall one-week performance (R 2 0.88–0.89; RMSE 30.6–31.3), significantly outperforming OLS (R 2 0.78; p < 0.0001) and GLM (R 2 0.79; p < 0.0001). Chronos outperformed other models in two-to-four-week performance. Chronos produced credible forecasts of the multivariate influenza surveillance predictions up to three weeks (R 2 ≥ 0.50; p < 0.05), whereas classical models fell below threshold beyond two weeks. TSFMs required as low as eight weeks of input data to achieve R 2 ≥ 0.50, compared to at least 297 weeks for classical models. TSFMs deliver comparatively more accurate, well-calibrated, and data-efficient epidemic forecasts, capturing temporal and inter-variable dependencies than classical regression models. Their ability to generate more reliable forecasts from minimal historical data compared to classical approaches supports their potential for rapid deployment in seasonal influenza surveillance and emerging pandemics such as COVID-19.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 准确的短期流感活动预测对于公共卫生准备工作至关重要,但对于依赖长期历史数据且经常因数据稀缺而失败的经典统计模型仍然具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们分析了香港(2014-2025年)605周的流感监测数据,包括就诊率、实验室检测、住院情况、重症病例和学校暴发。
elements_zh.methods: 将六种 TSFM(Google TimesFM、Amazon Chronos、IBM Granite Tiny Time Mixers [TTM]、Timer-XL、Moirai-MoE 和 UniTS)与滚动原点设计中的 OLS、GLM、SARIMA 和经验贝叶斯模型进行比较,生成一到四周的预测。使用 R2、RMSE、对称 MAPE、加权区间评分 (WIS) 和多变量残差诊断来评估预测准确性。
elements_zh.main_results: Chronos、TimesFM 和 SARIMA 取得了最佳整体一周表现(R2 0.88–0.89;RMSE 30.6–31.3),显着优于 OLS(R2 0.78;p < 0.0001)和 GLM(R2 0.79;p < 0.0001)。Chronos 在两到四周的表现中优于其他型号。Chronos 对长达三周的多变量流感 监测 预测进行了可靠的预测(R2 ≥ 0.50;p < 0.05),而经典模型在两周后下降到阈值以下。TSFM 只需 8 周的输入数据即可实现 R2 ≥ 0.50,而经典模型至少需要 297 周。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与经典回归模型相比,TSFM 可提供相对更准确、校准良好且数据高效的流行病预测,捕获时间和变量间的依赖性。与传统方法相比,它们能够从最少的历史数据中生成更可靠的预测,这支持了它们在 季节性流感 监测 和新出现的流行病(例如 COVID-19)中快速部署的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,TSFM 可以通过用最少的数据提供可靠的流感预测来加强公共卫生准备,从而在季节性 暴发 和大流行期间实现及时的资源分配和干预策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是使用来自单个地理区域(香港)的 监测 数据进行的,这可能会限制对具有不同流感动态的其他人群的普遍适用性。由于数据集规模大、比较设计严格以及具有统计显着性的结果,证据强度很高。

papers.title_zh: 使用时间序列基础模型进行多元流感预测:利用香港 11 年 监测 数据与经典统计模型的比较研究
papers.source_body_en: Accurate short-term forecasts of influenza activity are critical for public health preparedness but remain challenging with classical statistical models that depend on long historical data and often fail under data scarcity. Time-series foundation models (TSFMs), pretrained on large heterogeneous datasets, may offer improved accuracy and data efficiency through transferable temporal representations. We analyzed 605 weeks of influenza surveillance data from Hong Kong (2014–2025), including consultation rates, laboratory detections, hospital admissions, severe cases, and school outbreaks. Six TSFMs (Google TimesFM, Amazon Chronos, IBM Granite Tiny Time Mixers [TTM], Timer-XL, Moirai-MoE, and UniTS) were compared with OLS, GLM, SARIMA, and empirical Bayesian models in a rolling-origin design generating one- to four-week forecasts. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using R 2 , RMSE, symmetric MAPE, weighted interval score (WIS) and multivariable residual diagnostics. We further estimated the minimal input window required for R 2 ≥ 0.50 and the maximum credible forecast horizon (R 2 ≥ 0.50 with significant RMSE gain vs. Chronos, TimesFM, and SARIMA achieved the best overall one-week performance (R 2 0.88–0.89; RMSE 30.6–31.3), significantly outperforming OLS (R 2 0.78; p < 0.0001) and GLM (R 2 0.79; p < 0.0001). Chronos outperformed other models in two-to-four-week performance. Chronos produced credible forecasts of the multivariate influenza surveillance predictions up to three weeks (R 2 ≥ 0.50; p < 0.05), whereas classical models fell below threshold beyond two weeks. TSFMs required as low as eight weeks of input data to achieve R 2 ≥ 0.50, compared to at least 297 weeks for classical models. TSFMs deliver comparatively more accurate, well-calibrated, and data-efficient epidemic forecasts, capturing temporal and inter-variable dependencies than classical regression models. Their ability to generate more reliable forecasts from minimal historical data compared to classical approaches supports their potential for rapid deployment in seasonal influenza surveillance and emerging pandemics such as COVID-19.

papers.title: Maternal influenza vaccination boosts durable breast milk antibody-mediated protection in infants
papers.abstract: Influenza contributes to significant disease burden worldwide, and young infants are at an increased risk of severe influenza infection. Maternal antibodies transferred across the placenta and through breast milk confer anti-influenza immunity to the newborn. Placental transfer provides a finite window of protection, but breast milk antibody transfer may provide prolonged immunity across the postnatal period. Yet, how breastmilk antibody profiles are shaped by maternal vaccination, change postnatally, and whether they contribute to protection against influenza remains incompletely defined. Comprehensive systems serological analysis of influenza-specific antibodies across 21 different antigens in a longitudinal birth cohort revealed maternal influenza vaccination was associated with enhanced antibody-dependent complement deposition (ADCD) and FcγR binding in breast milk at two weeks postpartum. This effect was further stratified by trimester of vaccination: first trimester vaccinees exhibited increased ADCD and IgM levels, whereas second or third trimester vaccination was associated with increased FcγR and FcαR binding. Analysis of longitudinal samples revealed that anti-influenza antibody responses in milk shift postpartum toward increased FcγR binding and decreased ADCD activity and IgM levels. Finally, baseline ADCD activity in breast milk and serum IgG1 levels were identified as signatures of resistance to influenza infection during the first six months of life. A multivariate model combining correlates of protection across milk and serum compartments offered greater predictive power compared to either compartment alone, suggesting both routes of antibody transfer bolster anti-influenza immunity in infants. These data collectively suggest that maternal influenza vaccination confers infant protection via breast milk to augment placental antibody transfer, and the functional capacity of these protective antibodies could be enhanced with prolonged breastfeeding.

papers.title: The roles of pre-season immunity, age, viral shedding, and community exposures in shaping influenza household transmission dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract Our understanding of influenza transmission remains imperfect due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections that often go undetected. To address this challenge, we leveraged uniquely resolved data from a household cohort study spanning three consecutive years in rural and urban South Africa. The study incorporated pre-season serum collection and twice-weekly virological testing during the influenza season, regardless of symptom presence. We developed a subtype/lineage-specific influenza household transmission model that accounts for time-resolved viral shedding across the full clinical spectrum of infections, allowing us to disentangle the role of household and community exposures, pre-season immunity, and age on transmission. Our analysis revealed that viral shedding intensity, as measured by the cycle threshold (Ct) values of infected household members, significantly correlated with the risk of transmission for all four influenza subtypes/lineages. After adjusting for viral shedding, pre-season hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers greater than 1:40 were associated with a significantly lower risk of infection acquisition for A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, but not for B/Yamagata. Notably, children exhibited higher susceptibility and longer viral shedding durations compared to adults across all subtypes/lineages, even after adjusting for pre-season HAI titers. While our findings support that HAI titers correlate with protection, the strong residual effects of age on susceptibility and viral shedding may reflect the accumulation of additional immune responses shaped by repeated exposures over time. Our study underscores the need to explore immune mechanisms beyond HAI titers that modulate influenza susceptibility and transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses an incomplete understanding of influenza transmission dynamics, particularly the role of asymptomatic infections that often evade detection and the factors shaping household spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research used a household cohort study conducted over three consecutive influenza seasons in rural and urban South Africa, involving repeated pre-season serum collection and twice-weekly virological testing regardless of symptoms.
analysis.methods: A subtype/lineage-specific influenza household transmission model was developed to incorporate time-resolved viral shedding data across the full clinical spectrum of infections, enabling separation of household and community exposure effects, pre-season immunity, and age influences on transmission.
analysis.main_results: Viral shedding intensity, measured by cycle threshold values from infected household members, was significantly associated with increased transmission risk for all four influenza subtypes/lineages studied.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Pre-season hemagglutination inhibition titers above 1:40 were linked to lower infection risk for A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria but not B/Yamagata, while children showed higher susceptibility and longer shedding durations than adults across all subtypes, even after adjusting for pre-season immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of viral shedding intensity and age-specific susceptibility in influenza transmission, suggesting that immune mechanisms beyond hemagglutination inhibition titers may play key roles in modulating susceptibility and spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on abstract-only evidence and the absence of detailed methodological or statistical reporting, which constrains the strength of the conclusions drawn.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates influenza transmission dynamics within households in South Africa over three consecutive seasons, leveraging pre-season immunity data and twice-weekly virological testing to capture asymptomatic and symptomatic infections. Using a subtype-specific transmission model, the authors demonstrate that viral shedding intensity strongly correlates with transmission risk across all four influenza subtypes/lineages. Pre-season hemagglutination inhibition titers above 1:40 were associated with reduced infection risk for A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria but not B/Yamagata, while children exhibited higher susceptibility and prolonged shedding durations than adults, independent of pre-season immunity. These results underscore the need to explore immune mechanisms beyond hemagglutination inhibition titers and suggest that age-specific factors critically shape household transmission dynamics.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:我们对流感传播的理解仍然不完善,因为无症状感染的高患病率常常未被检测到。为应对这一挑战,我们利用了来自南非农村和城市地区连续三年的家庭队列研究研究中独特解析的数据。该研究纳入了季前血清采集和流感季节期间每周两次的病毒学检测,无论是否存在症状。我们开发了一种亚型/谱系特异性的流感家庭传播模型,该模型考虑了整个感染临床谱中的时间解析病毒脱落,使我们能够分离家庭和社区暴露、季前免疫力和年龄对传播的影响。我们的分析显示,受感染家庭成员的病毒脱落强度,以循环阈值(Ct)值衡量,与所有四种流感亚型/谱系的传播风险显著相关。在调整病毒脱落后,季前血凝抑制(HAI)滴度大于1:40与甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒和B/Victoria的感染获取风险显著降低相关,但对B/Yamagata则无此关联。值得注意的是,与成人相比,儿童在所有亚型/谱系中表现出更高的易感性和更长的病毒脱落持续时间,即使在调整了季前HAI滴度后也是如此。虽然我们的研究结果支持HAI滴度与保护作用相关,但年龄对易感性和病毒脱落的强烈残余效应可能反映了随时间推移反复暴露所形成的额外免疫应答的积累。我们的研究强调了需要探索超出HAI滴度的免疫机制,这些机制调节流感的易感性和传播。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the effect of pH on the solubilization of the influenza A viral core, addressing a gap in understanding how environmental factors influence viral structure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved an in vitro disassembly process of influenza A virus capsids using gradient centrifugation, conducted in a controlled laboratory setting.
analysis.methods: The methods included the use of gel electrophoresis and protein staining to visualize the disassembly of the viral core under varying acidic conditions.
analysis.main_results: Gel electrophoresis and protein staining revealed the progressive disassembly of the core structure under acidic conditions, with specific patterns observed at different pH levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of pH-induced structural changes in the viral core, offering a novel visualization technique for studying viral disassembly.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings contribute to the understanding of viral structural dynamics, which may inform future research on viral stability and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro conditions, and the evidence is based on visual observation rather than quantitative analysis, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the effect of pH on the solubilization of the influenza A viral core through an in vitro disassembly process. Using gel electrophoresis and protein staining, the authors observed progressive structural changes under acidic conditions, providing a novel visualization method. The findings enhance understanding of viral structural dynamics, which could support future research on viral stability and therapeutic development. However, the study's reliance on in vitro conditions and visual interpretation limits the strength of the evidence, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title: Development, applications, and future prospects of RNA virus reverse genetics technology
papers.abstract: Viral reverse genetics enables the rescue of infectious virions from cloned cDNA and serves as a core technique for mapping viral genotype–phenotype relationships, dissecting RNA viral life cycles, and developing antiviral countermeasures. This review systematically summarizes the evolution, technical framework and optimization strategies of RNA virus reverse genetics, with three prototype viruses covering all major RNA genome types: SARS-CoV-2 (+ssRNA), non-segmented negative-sense Newcastle disease virus (NDV), and segmented negative-sense influenza A virus. Core modules including infectious clone construction, diverse promoter systems, hammerhead/HDV ribozymes, and solutions for large unstable genomes such as BAC and ISA are elaborated. We summarize its irreplaceable applications in vaccine development, pathogenesis research, virus-host interaction analysis and high-throughput antiviral screening. Current bottlenecks include low rescue efficiency, cDNA genetic instability and biosafety hazards. We also introduce non-infectious surrogate platforms and establish a three-tier antiviral screening pipeline. Future advances will integrate CRISPR/Cas editing, standardized modular tools, biosafety engineering, AI and big data. Distinct from previous reviews focusing on single viral genera, this work conducts cross-type horizontal comparisons and summarizes universal technical obstacles and tailored optimizations, offering comprehensive references for basic virology, accelerated vaccine innovation and precise antiviral design.

papers.title_zh: RNA病毒反向遗传学技术的发展、应用及未来展望
papers.source_body_en: Viral reverse genetics enables the rescue of infectious virions from cloned cDNA and serves as a core technique for mapping viral genotype–phenotype relationships, dissecting RNA viral life cycles, and developing antiviral countermeasures. This review systematically summarizes the evolution, technical framework and optimization strategies of RNA virus reverse genetics, with three prototype viruses covering all major RNA genome types: SARS-CoV-2 (+ssRNA), non-segmented negative-sense Newcastle disease virus (NDV), and segmented negative-sense influenza A virus. Core modules including infectious clone construction, diverse promoter systems, hammerhead/HDV ribozymes, and solutions for large unstable genomes such as BAC and ISA are elaborated. We summarize its irreplaceable applications in vaccine development, pathogenesis research, virus-host interaction analysis and high-throughput antiviral screening. Current bottlenecks include low rescue efficiency, cDNA genetic instability and biosafety hazards. We also introduce non-infectious surrogate platforms and establish a three-tier antiviral screening pipeline. Future advances will integrate CRISPR/Cas editing, standardized modular tools, biosafety engineering, AI and big data. Distinct from previous reviews focusing on single viral genera, this work conducts cross-type horizontal comparisons and summarizes universal technical obstacles and tailored optimizations, offering comprehensive references for basic virology, accelerated vaccine innovation and precise antiviral design.

papers.title: Original Paper The influence of early influenza exposures on immunity in infants and children: The US Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Preprint)
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Influenza vaccine effectiveness is variable, while influenza morbidity and mortality remain high. Immunologic imprinting for influenza has been described and may contribute to suboptimal vaccine performance. Unfortunately, critical data are lacking on the natural history of influenza in pregnancy and childhood. Appropriately designed maternal-birth cohorts can identify the earliest exposures to influenza and are necessary to address gaps in influenza epidemiology and immunology that currently hinder our ability to develop more broadly effective and durable vaccines. OBJECTIVE We describe the protocol for the Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Immunological Memory to Prior INfluenza over Time), an intensive maternal-birth cohort, which aims to understand how early exposures to influenza antigens shape responses later in life. METHODS IMPRINT is a prospective birth cohort of healthy mothers and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mothers are enrolled in the third trimester and followed with their child for at least three years with an enrollment goal of 1,500 mother-child pairs. Starting in week 2 of life, weekly child nasal swabs and twice weekly symptom surveys are collected, regardless of the presence/absence of symptoms. Serum is collected from mothers at enrollment and each summer post-enrollment. Child blood samples are collected from the umbilical cord at delivery and from the child at week 6, every summer, and following influenza infection and vaccination. Whole blood, serum, plasma, and peripheral blood mononucleated cells are collected. Medical records are abstracted to capture clinical data on medically attended respiratory illness. Review of state registries and the medical record capture vaccine administration dates. Other collected specimens included stool, human milk, saliva, and cheek swabs. Epidemiologic, immunologic, and virologic studies are underway to determine how influenza exposures influence incidence, subclinical infection, symptomology, and immunologic responses to subsequent exposures. RESULTS Screening and enrollment began October 2019 and ended November 2025. In total, 1,624 mothers were provisionally enrolled in pregnancy and 1,324 met final eligibility criteria for study enrollment. Participant follow-up is on-going. Participants that met final eligibility requirements were significantly different from those that did not; enrolled mothers tended to be older, in a partnership, of white race and/or non-Hispanic ethnicity, have private insurance, higher household income, and more education. CONCLUSIONS IMPRINT integrates advanced methodologic, laboratory, and epidemiologic tools from a complimentary group of collaborators to detect and order influenza infections and vaccinations experienced in the first years of life. This cohort struggled to advance maternal-infant pairs through the eligibility run-in period but also demonstrated successful follow-up of those pairs that met eligibility in an intensive, multi-year study. IMPRINT provides a novel framework to improve understanding of the immunologic responses to primary influenza exposures and to describe how the initial exposure and the subsequent order of exposures impacts the influenza immune landscape. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05436184

papers.title_zh: 原始论文早期流感暴露对婴儿和儿童免疫力的影响:美国流感 IMPRINT 队列研究(预印本)
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Influenza vaccine effectiveness is variable, while influenza morbidity and mortality remain high. Immunologic imprinting for influenza has been described and may contribute to suboptimal vaccine performance. Unfortunately, critical data are lacking on the natural history of influenza in pregnancy and childhood. Appropriately designed maternal-birth cohorts can identify the earliest exposures to influenza and are necessary to address gaps in influenza epidemiology and immunology that currently hinder our ability to develop more broadly effective and durable vaccines. OBJECTIVE We describe the protocol for the Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Immunological Memory to Prior INfluenza over Time), an intensive maternal-birth cohort, which aims to understand how early exposures to influenza antigens shape responses later in life. METHODS IMPRINT is a prospective birth cohort of healthy mothers and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mothers are enrolled in the third trimester and followed with their child for at least three years with an enrollment goal of 1,500 mother-child pairs. Starting in week 2 of life, weekly child nasal swabs and twice weekly symptom surveys are collected, regardless of the presence/absence of symptoms. Serum is collected from mothers at enrollment and each summer post-enrollment. Child blood samples are collected from the umbilical cord at delivery and from the child at week 6, every summer, and following influenza infection and vaccination. Whole blood, serum, plasma, and peripheral blood mononucleated cells are collected. Medical records are abstracted to capture clinical data on medically attended respiratory illness. Review of state registries and the medical record capture vaccine administration dates. Other collected specimens included stool, human milk, saliva, and cheek swabs. Epidemiologic, immunologic, and virologic studies are underway to determine how influenza exposures influence incidence, subclinical infection, symptomology, and immunologic responses to subsequent exposures. RESULTS Screening and enrollment began October 2019 and ended November 2025. In total, 1,624 mothers were provisionally enrolled in pregnancy and 1,324 met final eligibility criteria for study enrollment. Participant follow-up is on-going. Participants that met final eligibility requirements were significantly different from those that did not; enrolled mothers tended to be older, in a partnership, of white race and/or non-Hispanic ethnicity, have private insurance, higher household income, and more education. CONCLUSIONS IMPRINT integrates advanced methodologic, laboratory, and epidemiologic tools from a complimentary group of collaborators to detect and order influenza infections and vaccinations experienced in the first years of life. This cohort struggled to advance maternal-infant pairs through the eligibility run-in period but also demonstrated successful follow-up of those pairs that met eligibility in an intensive, multi-year study. IMPRINT provides a novel framework to improve understanding of the immunologic responses to primary influenza exposures and to describe how the initial exposure and the subsequent order of exposures impacts the influenza immune landscape. papers.title: Patterns of the gut microbiota and metabolome as potential biomarkers associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional observational pilot study
papers.abstract: Immunogenicity to influenza vaccination is often impaired in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The role of the gut microbiota and its metabolic output in modulating this response remains underexplored. This study is the first to explore gut microbiota patterns and metabolites in response to influenza vaccination in patients with SLE. A cross-sectional observational pilot study was conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital between May 2021 and July 2022. Participants with SLE who had received either a boosted dose or a standard dose of a quadrivalent influenza vaccine were enrolled. We analyzed fecal 16 S rDNA and metabolomic profiles using liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry to identify signatures associated with seroconversion (determined using the hemagglutination inhibition assay). A total of 62 participants with SLE participated in the study, and 61 fecal samples were submitted for metabolomic analysis. Most participants were female (58/62, 93.6%). The median ages in the standard and booster dose groups were 35.5 (interquartile range 28–42.5) and 34 (25–43) years, respectively ( P = 0.878). The overall gut microbiota patterns were similar in both groups; however, the genus Bacteroides was significantly associated with seroconversion to A(H1N1) and A(H3N2) ( P < 0.05). Metabolomic analysis identified upregulation of 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol and L-cysteic acid in seroconverters, whereas neopterin was significantly elevated in nonresponders, furthermore, several bacterial taxa were correlated with these metabolites. The level of immunosuppressive treatment and the use of antimicrobials for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections affected influenza immunogenicity in this study population. Some metabolites also appeared to be linked to vaccine immunogenicity, although the underlying mechanism is unclear. Our findings identify specific gut microbial taxa and fecal metabolites, particularly 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol, which are significantly associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in SLE patients. These results suggest that the gut–immune axis may play a modulatory role in vaccine responses and may provide potential non-invasive biomarkers that can identify patients at risk of suboptimal influenza protection.

papers.title_zh: 肠道微生物群和代谢组的模式作为与系统性红斑狼疮中流感 疫苗 免疫原性相关的潜在生物标志物:横断面观察性试点研究
papers.source_body_en: Immunogenicity to influenza vaccination is often impaired in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The role of the gut microbiota and its metabolic output in modulating this response remains underexplored. This study is the first to explore gut microbiota patterns and metabolites in response to influenza vaccination in patients with SLE. A cross-sectional observational pilot study was conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital between May 2021 and July 2022. Participants with SLE who had received either a boosted dose or a standard dose of a quadrivalent influenza vaccine were enrolled. We analyzed fecal 16 S rDNA and metabolomic profiles using liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry to identify signatures associated with seroconversion (determined using the hemagglutination inhibition assay). A total of 62 participants with SLE participated in the study, and 61 fecal samples were submitted for metabolomic analysis. Most participants were female (58/62, 93.6%). The median ages in the standard and booster dose groups were 35.5 (interquartile range 28–42.5) and 34 (25–43) years, respectively ( P = 0.878). The overall gut microbiota patterns were similar in both groups; however, the genus Bacteroides was significantly associated with seroconversion to A(H1N1) and A(H3N2) ( P < 0.05). Metabolomic analysis identified upregulation of 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol and L-cysteic acid in seroconverters, whereas neopterin was significantly elevated in nonresponders, furthermore, several bacterial taxa were correlated with these metabolites. The level of immunosuppressive treatment and the use of antimicrobials for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections affected influenza immunogenicity in this study population. Some metabolites also appeared to be linked to vaccine immunogenicity, although the underlying mechanism is unclear. Our findings identify specific gut microbial taxa and fecal metabolites, particularly 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol, which are significantly associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in SLE patients. These results suggest that the gut–immune axis may play a modulatory role in vaccine responses and may provide potential non-invasive biomarkers that can identify patients at risk of suboptimal influenza protection.

papers.full_text: Lab Animal | Volume 55 | August 2026 | 285 285 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41684-026-01776-9 Research highlights lab animal Infectious disease New knockout mice for influenza research Because viruses depend on host cells for the energy and resources needed to replicate and spread, extensive research has been devoted to identifying host factors that facilitate infection. Although these studies, including numerous in vitro screens, have uncovered hundreds of human genes that may contribute to viral replication, they do not fully capture the complexity of infection in vivo. To address this limitation, a team of researchers generated a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knock- out mice and used it to identify host genes that influence susceptibility to influenza A virus infection in vivo. To prioritize candidate genes for in vivo analysis, the researchers employed a multi-step screening strategy. They first compiled 386 candidate genes from a protein interactome study and a large-scale meta-analysis. After excluding genes essential for survival, they narrowed the list to 290 can- didates. Next, they conducted an siRNA-based functional screen in influenza A virus-infected mouse L929 cells, identifying 148 genes with potential roles in viral replication. From these candidates, the team successfully generated 84 knockout mouse lines. The team challenged the 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pan- demic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04. They monitored survival and body weight for 14 days and calculated enhanced protective efficacy (EPE) relative to wild-type (WT) controls. Using a threshold of an average EPE of at least 25% across two or more independ- ent trials, they identified 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance to infection. Notably, several host factors exhibited sex-specific effects, revealing differences in male and female responses that were not apparent in cell culture studies. Among the strongest candidates, Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showed robust protec- tion in both sexes. Although the molecular mechanisms remain unclear, these findings provide a valuable resource of validated host targets for future antiviral therapeutic development. Alexandra Le Bras Original reference: Ueki, H. et al. analysis.research_question_and_background: Because viruses depend on host cells for replication and spread, extensive research has identified host factors that facilitate infection, but these studies do not fully capture the complexity of infection in vivo.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A team of researchers generated a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knockout mice and used it to identify host genes that influence susceptibility to influenza A virus infection in vivo.
analysis.methods: They compiled 386 candidate genes from a protein interactome study and meta-analysis, narrowed the list to 290 after excluding essential genes, conducted an siRNA-based functional screen in influenza A virus-infected mouse L929 cells, and generated 84 knockout mouse lines.
analysis.main_results: After challenging the 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pandemic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04, they identified 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance to infection, with Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showing robust protection in both sexes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Although the molecular mechanisms remain unclear, these findings provide a valuable resource of validated host targets for future antiviral therapeutic development and reveal sex-specific effects not apparent in cell culture studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identified host factors could inform the development of novel antiviral therapies and highlight the importance of considering sex-specific responses in influenza research.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate due to the use of a single mouse-adapted strain and the unclear molecular mechanisms, though the large-scale in vivo screening approach provides robust data.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the limitation of in vitro studies by generating a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knockout mice to identify host genes influencing influenza A virus susceptibility in vivo. The researchers screened 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pandemic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04, identifying 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance. Notably, Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showed robust protection in both sexes, while other factors exhibited sex-specific effects. These findings provide a valuable resource for antiviral therapeutic development, though the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. The study highlights the importance of in vivo models and sex-specific responses in influenza research.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于病毒依赖于 宿主 细胞进行复制和传播,因此广泛的研究已经确定了促进感染的 宿主 因子,但这些研究并未完全捕获体内感染的复杂性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一组研究人员生成了一个 CRISPR-Cas9 基因敲除小鼠文库,并用它来识别影响体内甲型流感病毒感染易感性的 宿主 基因。
elements_zh.methods: 他们从蛋白质相互作用组研究和荟萃分析中汇编了 386 个候选基因,在排除必需基因后将列表缩小到 290 个,在甲型流感病毒感染的小鼠 L929 细胞中进行了基于 siRNA 的功能筛选,并产生了 84 个敲除小鼠系。
elements_zh.main_results: 在用致死剂量的小鼠适应的甲型H1N1流行性流感病毒株MA-CA04攻击84个小鼠品系后,他们鉴定出17个基因修饰的品系具有增强的感染抵抗力,其中Arhgef28和Lasp1修饰的小鼠在两性中都显示出强大的保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管分子机制仍不清楚,但这些发现为未来 宿主 治疗开发提供了经过验证的 宿主 靶标的宝贵资源,并揭示了细胞培养研究中不明显的性别特异性效应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 确定的 宿主 因子可以为新型 抗病毒药物 疗法的开发提供信息,并强调在流感研究中考虑性别特异性反应的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管大规模体内筛选方法提供了可靠的数据,但由于使用了单一的小鼠适应菌株和不清楚的分子机制,该研究的证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于病毒依赖于 宿主 细胞进行复制和传播,因此广泛的研究已经确定了促进感染的 宿主 因子,但这些研究并未完全捕获体内感染的复杂性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一组研究人员生成了一个 CRISPR-Cas9 基因敲除小鼠文库,并用它来识别影响体内甲型流感病毒感染易感性的 宿主 基因。
analysis_zh.methods: 他们从蛋白质相互作用组研究和荟萃分析中汇编了 386 个候选基因,在排除必需基因后将列表缩小到 290 个,在甲型流感病毒感染的小鼠 L929 细胞中进行了基于 siRNA 的功能筛选,并产生了 84 个敲除小鼠系。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在用致死剂量的小鼠适应的甲型H1N1流行性流感病毒株MA-CA04攻击84个小鼠品系后,他们鉴定出17个基因修饰的品系具有增强的感染抵抗力,其中Arhgef28和Lasp1修饰的小鼠在两性中都显示出强大的保护作用。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管分子机制仍不清楚,但这些发现为未来 宿主 治疗开发提供了经过验证的 宿主 靶标的宝贵资源,并揭示了细胞培养研究中不明显的性别特异性效应。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 确定的 宿主 因子可以为新型 抗病毒药物 疗法的开发提供信息,并强调在流感研究中考虑性别特异性反应的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管大规模体内筛选方法提供了可靠的数据,但由于使用了单一的小鼠适应菌株和不清楚的分子机制,该研究的证据强度中等。

papers.title: Analysis of the pathogen spectrum, co-infection characteristics, and risk of severe disease in community-acquired pneumonia among children in Henan province
papers.abstract: Objective To analyze the pathogen spectrum, co-infection characteristics, and risk factors for severe pneumonia in children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Henan Province. Methods This study included 2,149 pediatric inpatients with CAP admitted to the Third Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University from June 2023 to June 2025. Throat swab samples were tested using multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for 11 respiratory pathogens. Combined with culture results, the pathogen spectrum and co-infection characteristics were analyzed, and risk factors for severe pneumonia were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis. It should be noted that a positive throat-swab PCR result cannot unambiguously differentiate pathogenic infection from colonization, prior infection, or asymptomatic carriage; this inherent limitation was taken into account during data interpretation. Results The overall pathogen detection rate was 89.34%, with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (31.55%) and rhinovirus (31.13%) predominating; among bacteria, Haemophilus influenzae (3.77%) and Streptococcus pneumoniae (3.35%) were the most common. Except for influenza B virus and human coronavirus, significant differences were observed in the age distribution of each pathogen ( P < 0.05). The detection rate of M. pneumoniae increased significantly with age, reaching 58.5% in school-aged children. Rhinovirus was active throughout the year (peaking at 65.14% in October 2024), while M. pneumoniae had the highest detection rate in October 2023 (65.93%). The overall co-infection rate was 31.07%, consisting primarily of virus–virus or virus–atypical pathogen combinations (21.49%), with rhinovirus– M. pneumoniae being the most common (8.52%). Independent risk factors for severe pneumonia were underlying medical conditions (OR = 4.031) and a history of preterm birth (OR = 3.544), whereas co-infections with viruses or atypical pathogens, or concurrent bacterial infections, did not significantly increase the risk of severe disease. Conclusion From June 2023 to June 2025, the pathogen spectrum of CAP in children in Henan Province was dominated by M. pneumoniae and rhinovirus (though HRV positivity should be interpreted with caution given its high asymptomatic carriage rate), with a distinct age distribution. Underlying medical conditions and a history of preterm birth were the primary risk factors for severe pneumonia.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的分析河南省社区获得性肺炎(CAP)儿童重症肺炎的病原谱、合并感染特征及危险因素。方法本研究纳入2023年6月至2025年6月郑州大学第三附属医院收治的2149名CAP儿科住院患者,采用多重聚合酶链反应(PCR)对咽拭子样本进行11种呼吸道病原体检测。结合培养结果,分析病原谱和合并感染特征,并采用多元Logistic回归分析确定重症肺炎的危险因素。值得注意的是,咽拭子 PCR 阳性结果不能明确区分病原体感染与定植、既往感染或无症状携带;在数据解释过程中考虑到了这种固有的局限性。结果病原菌总体检出率为89.34%,以肺炎支原体(31.55%)和鼻病毒(31.13%)为主;细菌中,流感嗜血杆菌(3.77%)和肺炎链球菌(3.35%)最为常见。除乙型流感病毒和人类冠状病毒外,各病原体的年龄分布均存在显着差异( P < 0.05)。肺炎支原体检出率随着年龄的增长而显着升高,学龄儿童中肺炎支原体检出率达到58.5%。鼻病毒全年活跃(2024年10月达到峰值65.14%),而肺炎支原体检出率最高的是2023年10月(65.93%)。总体混合感染率为31.07%,主要由病毒-病毒或病毒-非典型病原体组合组成(21.49%),其中鼻病毒-肺炎支原体最为常见(8.52%)。重症肺炎的独立危险因素是基础疾病(OR = 4.031)和早产史(OR = 3.544),而病毒或非典型病原体合并感染或并发细菌感染并不会显着增加重症风险。结论 2023年6月至2025年6月,河南省儿童CAP病原谱以肺炎支原体和鼻病毒为主(HRV阳性无症状携带率较高,需谨慎解读),年龄分布明显。基础疾病和早产史是重症肺炎的主要危险因素。

papers.title: High-efficiency upconversion luminescent quenching via defect-engineered Cu 3− x P for dual-aptamers-mediated tri-modal H1N1 lateral flow immunoassay
papers.abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Influenza A virus is critical for influenza prevention and control by reducing severe illness and mortality. However, conventional lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is limited by low sensitivity, and luminescent LFIA is short of significant signal changes at low target concentrations. Herein, a luminescence quenching LFIA platform is developed by integrating upconversion nanoparticles, defect engineered Cu3−xP, and dual aptamers to address above bottleneck via a synergistic mechanism. Density functional theory calculations indicate that in the new type Cu3−xP quencher, Cu vacancies induce new electronic states at the valence band edge and create extra electron transition pathway, which boost Förster Resonance Energy Transfer and upconversion luminescence quenching efficiency. Therefore, the test line luminescence signal is effectively suppressed to establish a sensitive luminescence quenching LFIA, which is sensitive to signal changes. Cu3−xP also exhibits broad ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) absorption for colorimetric and photothermal signals. The synergy luminescence-colorimetry-photothermal tri-modal analytical platform achieves a limit of detection of 0.907 ng/mL for H1N1 hemagglutinin. Moreover, two selected aptamers with stable and non-overlapping binding sites verified by molecular docking are critical for forming a sandwich structure, enabling high sensitivity toward H1N1 over H7N9, H9N2, H6N1, H7N7, and H5N1, along with good anti-interference ability. This work provides a scalable point of care influenza detection strategy balancing sensitivity and specificity, optimizing LFIA for on site viral diagnostics.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 甲型流感病毒的早期 诊断 对于减少重症和 诊断 流感预防和控制至关重要。然而,传统的侧流免疫分析(LFIA)由于灵敏度低而受到限制,而发光LFIA在低目标浓度下缺乏显着的信号变化。在此,通过集成上转换纳米粒子、缺陷工程 Cu3−xP 和双适体,开发了发光猝灭 LFIA 平台,以通过协同机制解决上述瓶颈。密度泛函理论计算表明,在新型 Cu3−xP 猝灭剂中,Cu 空位在价带边缘诱导新的电子态并产生额外的电子跃迁路径,从而提高福斯特共振能量转移和上转换发光猝灭效率。因此,有效抑制测试线发光信号,建立灵敏的发光猝灭LFIA,对信号变化敏感。Cu3−xP 还对色度和光热信号表现出广泛的紫外可见 (UV-vis) 吸收。协同发光-比色-光热三模式分析平台实现了 H1N1 血凝素的检测限为 0.907 ng/mL。此外,通过分子对接验证的两个具有稳定且不重叠结合位点的适配体对于形成夹心结构至关重要,使得对H1N1的敏感性高于H7N9、H9N2、H6N1、H7N7和H5N1,并且具有良好的抗干扰能力。这项工作提供了一种可扩展的护理点流感检测策略,平衡了灵敏度和特异性,优化了 LFIA 进行现场病毒诊断。
papers.summary_zh: 摘要 甲型流感病毒的早期 诊断 对于减少重症和 诊断 流感预防和控制至关重要。然而,传统的侧流免疫分析(LFIA)由于灵敏度低而受到限制,而发光LFIA在低目标浓度下缺乏显着的信号变化。在此,通过集成上转换纳米粒子、缺陷工程 Cu3−xP 和双适体,开发了发光猝灭 LFIA 平台,以通过协同机制解决上述瓶颈。密度泛函理论计算表明,在新型 Cu3−xP 猝灭剂中,Cu 空位在价带边缘诱导新的电子态并产生额外的电子跃迁路径,从而提高福斯特共振能量转移和上转换发光猝灭效率。因此,有效抑制测试线发光信号,建立灵敏的发光猝灭LFIA,对信号变化敏感。Cu3−xP 还对色度和光热信号表现出广泛的紫外可见 (UV-vis) 吸收。协同发光-比色-光热三模式分析平台实现了 H1N1 血凝素的检测限为 0.907 ng/mL。此外,通过分子对接验证的两个具有稳定且不重叠结合位点的适配体对于形成夹心结构至关重要,使得对H1N1的敏感性高于H7N9、H9N2、H6N1、H7N7和H5N1,并且具有良好的抗干扰能力。这项工作提供了一种可扩展的护理点流感检测策略,平衡了灵敏度和特异性,优化了 LFIA 进行现场病毒诊断。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一种发光猝灭侧流免疫分析 (LFIA) 平台,使用上转换纳米粒子、缺陷工程 Cu3−xP 和双适体检测 H1N1。
analysis_zh.methods: 该平台集成了上转换纳米颗粒、缺陷工程 Cu3−xP 和双适体,通过福斯特共振能量转移实现发光猝灭,并通过分子对接验证适体结合位点。
analysis_zh.main_results: 三模式分析平台对 H1N1 血凝素的检测限达到 0.907 ng/mL,对 H1N1 的灵敏度高于 H7N9、H9N2、H6N1、H7N7 和 H5N1。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将发光、比色法和光热信号的协同作用解释为一种可扩展的护理点流感检测策略,优化 LFIA 以进行现场病毒诊断。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作为流感提供了一种敏感且具体的护理点检测策略,改善了现场病毒诊断,并有可能通过早期 诊断 减少严重疾病和 诊断。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度很高,因为该研究提出了一种新颖的三模式平台,具有低检测限和经过验证的特异性,尽管仅抽象的证据限制了对现实世界适用性的评估。

To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk. Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-reports-2026-to-2027-season/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-report-30-july-2026-week-31 This report summarises the information from the surveillance systems which are used to monitor COVID-19 (caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)), influenza, and diseases caused by seasonal respiratory viruses in England. The report is based on data up to week 30 of 2026 between 20 July and 26 July 2026. Main points The main messages of this report are: influenza activity remained low and circulating at baseline levels COVID-19 activity remained low and circulating at baseline levels respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity remained low and circulating at baseline levels Seasonal reports Annual reports for the 2025 to 2026 season: Influenza in the UK, annual epidemiological report: winter 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Epidemiology of COVID-19 in England (published 25 June 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in all GP patients: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in school-aged children: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in frontline healthcare workers: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Summary of all respiratory virus activity Influenza activity Influenza activity remained low and is circulating at baseline levels. Emergency department (ED) attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) remained low. Reporting of weekly influenza hospital admissions for the 2025 to 2026 season concluded in week 17. Indicator Trend Level [note 1] Comments Laboratory surveillance Increasing Baseline Influenza positivity increased with a positivity rate on the most recent Sunday of 0.8% compared with 0.7% on the previous Sunday GP swabbing positivity Increasing Baseline In week 29, among all tested samples, 5% were positive for influenza, compared with 0.9% in the previous week COVID-19 activity COVID-19 activity remained low and is circulating at baseline levels. ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness remained low. Indicator Trend Level [note 1] Comments Laboratory surveillance Increasing Baseline COVID-19 PCR (polymerase chain reaction) positivity in hospital settings increased with a positivity rate on the most recent Sunday of 1.1% compared with 0.9% on the previous Sunday GP swabbing positivity Increasing Baseline In week 29, among all tested samples, 3% were positive for SARS-CoV-2, compared with 2.6% in the previous week Hospital admissions Remained low Baseline The overall weekly hospital admission rate for COVID-19 remained low at 0.15 per 100,000 compared with 0.13 per 100,000 in the previous week Respiratory syncytial virus activity RSV activity remained low and is circulating at baseline levels. ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis remained low. Reporting of weekly RSV hospital admissions for the 2025 to 2026 season concluded in week 14. Indicator Trend Level [note 1] Comments Laboratory surveillance Stable Baseline RSV positivity remained stable at 0.3% compared with 0.4% in the previous week. GP swabbing positivity Stable Baseline In week 29, among all tested samples, 0% were positive for RSV compared with 0% in the previous week Other viruses Indicator Trend Level [note 1] Comments Adenovirus Decreasing Baseline Adenovirus positivity (laboratory surveillance) decreased to 1.9% compared with 2.6% in the previous week Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) Decreasing Baseline hMPV positivity (laboratory surveillance) decreased to 0.1% compared with 0.3% in the previous week Parainfluenza Decreasing Baseline Parainfluenza positivity (laboratory surveillance) decreased to 1.5% compared with 1.9% in the previous week Rhinovirus Increasing slightly Baseline Rhinovirus positivity (laboratory surveillance) increased slightly to 9.5% compared with 9% in the previous week Note 1: these indicators use the moving epidemic method (MEM) and the mean standard deviation method (MSD) to define thresholds to determine their respective levels of activity. Further information on these methods can be found in Influenza surveillance in Europe: establishing epidemic thresholds by the Moving Epidemic Method and Setting thresholds to determine COVID-19 activity levels using the mean standard deviation (MSD) method, England, 2022 to 2024. The MEM approach is well-established for some influenza surveillance indicators, however, for other indicators both the MEM and MSD are experimental and may be subject to future revision. Influenza laboratory surveillance and GP swabbing positivity have transitioned from using MEM to using MSD. These approaches will be considered alongside expert opinion and triangulation of other data sources. Laboratory surveillance Laboratory-confirmed cases The Second Generation Surveillance System (SGSS) captures test result information for notifiable infectious diseases, including COVID-19 and influenza, from laboratories in England. The unified sample dataset (USD) stores all SARS-CoV-2 test results reported to SGSS, Respiratory DataMart and UKHSA laboratories, and is used to calculate the percentage of tests positive for SARS-CoV-2 among all SARS-CoV-2 tests conducted. SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) PCR positivity in hospital settings increased in week 30, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 1.1% up to Sunday 26 July 2026. This is compared with 0.9% on the previous Sunday. Influenza positivity in week 30 increased, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 0.8% up to Sunday 26 July 2026, compared with 0.7% on the previous Sunday. Due to an ongoing data quality issue resulting in more tests than usual being removed, historical positivity for influenza may be slightly lower in reports published from week 25 2025 onwards. Historical estimates will be updated once the affected data has been rectified. Figure 1. Rolling 7-day positivity of tests positive for SARS-CoV-2 among all reported SARS-CoV-2 tests, England 2022 to present [note 2] [note 3] Note 2: data from previous seasons is aligned by day. Note 3: testing policy and practice may change over time which can impact positivity rates, therefore comparisons over time should be interpreted with caution. Notable changes in testing policy occurred during 2022 to 2023, which are outlined in the data quality report. Figure 2. Rolling 7-day positivity of tests positive for influenza among all reported influenza tests, England 2022 to present [note 2] Note 2: data from previous seasons is aligned by day. Respiratory DataMart System Respiratory DataMart is a sentinel laboratory-based surveillance system where participating laboratories report positive and negative test results for a number of respiratory viruses from samples primarily taken in hospital. A small proportion of primary care samples are also included in this reporting. In week 30, data is based on reporting from 9 out of the 14 sentinel laboratories. In week 30, 2,561 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for influenza. There were 12 positive samples for influenza: 7 influenza A (not subtyped), 2 influenza A (H3N2), 0 influenza A (H1N1)pdm09, and 3 influenza B. Overall, influenza positivity decreased to 0.5% in week 30 compared with 0.8% in the previous week. In week 30, 3,224 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for SARS-CoV-2. There were 33 positive samples for SARS-CoV-2. SARS-CoV-2 positivity increased to 1% compared with 0.6% in the previous week, with the highest positivity in those aged between 15 and 44 years at 1.4%. RSV positivity remained stable at 0.3%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 1.5%. Adenovirus positivity decreased to 1.9%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 5 and 14 years at 12.3%. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) positivity decreased to 0.1%, with the highest positivity in those aged 80 years and over at 0.5%. Parainfluenza positivity decreased to 1.5%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 15 and 44 years at 1.9%. analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency's weekly surveillance report for 30 July 2026 (week 31) indicates low activity for influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in England. Influenza positivity rates remained at baseline levels (0.8% in labs, 5% in GP swabs), while COVID-19 PCR positivity in hospitals slightly increased to 1.1%. Hospital admissions for COVID-19 were low at 0.15 per 100,000. Other viruses like adenovirus and human metapneumovirus showed decreasing trends, with rhinovirus slightly increasing. The report uses experimental methods (MEM/MSD) for some indicators, and data remains provisional. No significant public health impact or elevated risk was identified.

competition on influenza and COVID-19 prevention and control 3 August – 13 September 2026 Reading time: 2 min (484 words) العربية Français Русский Español WHO invites students and young professionals to participate in this youth competition by developing brief videos that highlight the importance of influenza and/or COVID-19 prevention and control. The videos are encouraged to be innovative, address misinformation/myths, and encourage their community to protect themselves from seasonal influenza and COVID-19. Competition theme: “How do you shield your circle from respiratory infections, like influenza and COVID-19?” Eligibility: Participants must be students or young professionals between the ages of 18 and 35. Competition Prompts: The submission must include a brief video that responds to one or more of the following prompts: Prompt 1: Who needs protection from seasonal influenza/COVID-19? How can vulnerable groups protect themselves? Why is it important? Prompt 2: How do you respond to someone who has doubts about influenza and/or COVID-19 prevention and control in your community? Prompt 3: What myths about influenza and/or COVID-19 prevention and control are circulating in your community? How do you address them? Instructions for participants: Participants must address at least one of the competition prompts in their video. Students can work independently or in teams. Video can be a maximum of 90 seconds (1.5 minutes). Students can submit up to three videos. Submitted videos are encouraged to be creative. Video styles can include but are not limited to storytelling, interview, reel, animation, drawings, poem, dialogue, or other creative formats. If AI is used to generate any portion of the submission, it must be acknowledged in the submission form. The video may be in any language but must include English subtitles. Submissions will be assessed on the following criteria: Video message aligns with the competition theme and responds to at least one of the competition prompts Originality and creativity Accuracy and clarity of health information Visual style and storytelling quality The video includes English subtitles Responses to the submission form questions including the: Motivation/rationale for the video Prompts selected and how they were addressed Potential impact of the video Feasibility for dissemination in the community Confirmation that all filmed individuals consented to their appearance in the video and are over the age of 18 Confirmation that the individuals submitting the video are between the ages of 18-35 years Timeline: The competition and the submission form open on Monday 3 August 2026. All submissions must be received through the designated Microsoft Forms by Sunday 13 September 2026 at 23:45 CEST. Review process: WHO subject matter experts will review and assess the videos using a designated rubric. WHO will notify the winner(s) in October 2026. Winning videos: There will be one global winning video and up to six videos highlighted as runners-up. The winning videos will be featured by WHO on the competition webpage. The student(s) who submitted the winning video will: Be invited to present their video on a global influenza/COVID-19 prevention and control-focused webinar in October 2026 and Receive a certificate from WHO featuring their name(s) and the video title Related Video submission form (open 3 August–13 September): LINK Fact sheets Influenza (seasonal) 28 February 2025 Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) 27 November 2025
